correctness.rationale: For fixed disjoint subsets totaling s labels, the exact joint-block probability is B_(n-s)/B_n; the Bell ratio is asymptotic to (W(n)/n)^s. Counting r-subsets by minimum position gives left test-window means (b-a)/(r-1)! and right means (b^r-a^r)/r!. For every fixed mixed factorial moment, overlapping candidate tuples are asymptotically negligible: early minima ranges diverge, terminal candidates spread over n/W(n), and left–right intersection probability tends to zero. Multivariate factorial moments therefore factor into Poisson moments, producing the joint point process and gap laws. The finite standalone checker establishes 520 exact rational partition, expectation and covariance identities for n<=8; it is not presented as an infinite proof.

evidence: Arratia–Tavaré, Adv. Math. 104 (1994), 90–154; accessible arXiv:1308.3279, Sections 5.3, 6 and 10.1, provides conditioned independent component-size processes with Poisson means W(n)^i/i!, plus refinement by component type.
Goh–Schmutz, Random Set Partitions, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 7 (1994), 419–436, abstract studies maximal block sizes and multiplicities.
DeSalvo–Menz, arXiv:1610.07664v1, primary MSC 60F05, Sections 2.2 and 5.5, extends component-size approximation methods but does not state labeled minimum-position point processes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 1994 independent-component comparison is the strongest structural predecessor. It controls unlabeled size profiles, not boundary point processes of minimum labels. Its formula for size-r block counts, followed by uniform-label assignment, suggests but does not itself state or logically force the exact joint two-boundary marked Poisson statement without a separate spatial argument; its general assembly approximations have not been exhaustively examined for an equivalent corollary.

value.rationale: The minimum label of a fixed-cardinality block is a canonical feature of an exchangeable set partition; its extremal law measures when a specific block size first and last appears along labels. The result identifies two distinct logarithmic scales, a size-indexed Weibull family, and full two-sided multitype independence. None of these calibrations follows from the asymptotic total counts alone; joint process convergence describes all extreme order statistics, rather than an isolated routine expectation.
